newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Old Mutual to keep foreign investment at limit.
newsitem.headline: Old Mutual to keep foreign investment at limit.

text.p: Old Mutual, South Africa's biggest investment company, said on Monday it had taken full advantage of the government's foreign investment concession for its Global Equity Fund and would continue to do so.
Old Mutual Unit Trusts managing director Selwyn Feldman on Monday reported record sales of 2.2 billion rand for the 12 months to the end of June.
The group ended the year with total assets of nine billion rand, he said.
Feldman told Reuters the group's Global Equity Fund had taken up the full amount allowed to be invested offshore through asset swaps.
In September last year, the central Reserve Bank allowed portfolio foreign investment of up to 10 percent of total funds via asset swaps.

"We have about 27 million rand in foreign assets, of which 21 million by book value is as a result of asset swaps," Feldman said, adding that the remainder of the fund's foreign holding was part of a sterling bond issue.
"We envisage increasing our equity holdings in the United States, the U.K. and Japan through asset swaps to keep the exposure at the very limit of that allowed," he said.
Old Mutual overseas investment manager Kevin Carter had been given a free hand to manage offshore investments "provided they are benchmarked only against the world index", he said.
Feldman said he hoped for a further relaxation of exchange controls on South African funds as soon as possible, but at least within the next 18 months.
"We would hope to be able to significantly expand our foreign investment within the next 12 to 18 months," he said.
"We see the current market cycle as a buying opportunity ahead of the expected upturn in 1997 and 1998," he said.
Feldman said Old Mutual expected to launch a money market fund next year, following passage of enabling legislation through parliament this year and the promulgation of rules.
